source_limit: Ruger's contemporary bird's-eye lithograph supports a varied low-rise city with frame dwellings, masonry business blocks and industrial buildings. Colbert and Chamberlin (1871, pp. 146-147) report a spring 1868 enumeration of 35,654 wooden buildings to 3,712 of brick and stone, so frame forms dominate outside the business centre. Neither source establishes these footprints, storey heights, window patterns, colours or individual addresses. Pre-fire stereographs of Lake, State and Clark streets (NYPL Dennis collection, Carbutt's Views of Chicago) show the business streets built wall to wall in Italianate and commercial-palace fronts of brick, pale stone and painted brick, with cast-iron storefronts, signboards, awnings, hooded and arched windows and bracketed cornices, and North Side houses behind fenced yards with stoops; they inform these period forms, not any generated front. Every kit dimension and facade is a bounded reconstruction, and no template represents a named building.

citations.citation: A New Map of Chicago. Chicago Evening Post, April 9, 1869. Reproduced with publication attribution on Chicagology, Ward Map – 2 February 1869.
what_it_supplies: Stepped municipal shape: Fullerton east of Western, North Avenue toward the new western limit, the canal southwest edge and Egan Avenue south.
A proposed Jefferson addition north of North Avenue and west of Western, distinguished from present city limits.
what_it_does_not_supply: Surveyed legal-boundary vertices, precise street positions or a reliable population count from the modern host paragraph.

citations.citation: Chicago Board of Public Works. Tenth Annual Report to the Common Council, for the municipal year ending March 31, 1871. Chicago, 1871.
what_it_supplies: Bridge existence, construction years, reported lengths and March 31 traffic counts. Madison bridge is specified as all iron; others distinguish wooden or iron chords.
Contracted sidewalk work, park improvements and canal-opening chronology.
what_it_does_not_supply: October 8 operating conditions, Sunday traffic volume, exact truss members, road widths or continuous pavement on every block.

citations.citation: Elias Colbert and Everett Chamberlin, Chicago and the Great Conflagration. Cincinnati and New York: C. F. Vent; Chicago: J. S. Goodman & Co., 1871.
what_it_supplies: A citywide ratio of building materials before the fire: in spring 1868, 35,654 wooden buildings to 3,712 of brick and stone (about nine in ten wooden).
The city's 59,500 buildings in 1871 by division, with the West Division largest (29,400).
Descriptions that the West Side's burned blocks were nearly all frame, and that the South Division's burned centre held the city's most expensive structures.
what_it_does_not_supply: A material for any particular lot, block or street; a material ratio by division or for 1871 itself; paint colours.

citations.citation: Edwards’ Annual Directory of the City of Chicago, 1871. Fourteenth annual issue. Chicago: Richard Edwards, 1871.
